assertion.name: Extrachromosomal MYCN Amplicon Architecture
assertion.description: In MYCN-amplified neuroblastoma the supernumerary MYCN copies are commonly carried on extrachromosomal circular DNA (ecDNA), which can be highly rearranged. The extrachromosomal form is the common state and not the only one: the same paper reports a MYCN amplicon carried as a linear intrachromosomal array, a homogeneously staining region. Amplicon composition is not random. Across a copy-number meta-dataset of 240 MYCN-amplified neuroblastomas, a 290 kb region downstream of MYCN was co-amplified in more than 90% of tumours, and the distal MYCN-specific enhancer e4, driven by the noradrenergic core regulatory circuit (CRC), lay inside the consensus amplicon in 90% of cases. Two amplicon classes follow. The first always co-amplifies a proximal CRC-driven enhancer; the second is structurally complex, lacks the key local enhancers and instead carries distal chromosomal fragments harbouring CRC-driven enhancers, which the authors read as ectopic enhancer hijacking replacing the missing local elements. That classification was made on primary-tumour copy-number profiles, which cannot separate extrachromosomal from intrachromosomal amplicons, so it applies to both forms. The two classes were prognostically indistinguishable in the same series, so amplicon class sets the regulatory route to MYCN overexpression rather than clinical behaviour. Separately, rearrangements derived from extrachromosomal circles can give rise to cancer-causing lesions and are associated with adverse clinical outcome; that association belongs to the circle-derived rearrangements and not to amplicon class.

assertion.name: Primary Tumor Growth and Local Mass Effect
assertion.description: Growth of the primary tumor at its site of origin along the sympathetic nervous system, and the pressure it exerts on, or its growth into, neighboring structures. About three-quarters of primary tumors arise in the abdomen or pelvis, half of these in the adrenal medulla, about a fifth in the posterior mediastinum and about a twentieth in the neck, and the local signs follow from the site. An abdominal primary can present as a palpable abdominal mass, abdominal distension or abdominal pain. A paravertebral tumor can grow through the neural foramina into the spinal canal and compress the spinal cord or nerve roots. Horner syndrome is seen mostly with localized disease, often with cervical or thoracic tumors, and is attributed to mass effect of the tumor on the sympathetic innervation of the eye. Compression of the renal artery or renal parenchyma is the usual explanation offered for hypertension at diagnosis, but a registry survey of hypertensive children could not demonstrate a correlation between hypertension and compression of the renal vascular pedicle. Cells leaving the primary tumor give rise to metastases at distant sites.
assertion.notes: The node has no upstream edge from Unlimited Replicative Potential: neuroblastomas with a favorable prognosis expand clonally after a short evolution, whereas aggressive ones acquire telomere maintenance mechanisms during a prolonged evolution (PMID:36973454), so a primary tumor can grow without one.
